title: Intake Air Temperature (IAT) Sensor
introduction:
This procedure applies to the 2.3L EcoBoost (231kW/314PS). I use the ribbed intake hose as the landmark: the IAT sensor fits into the neighboring smooth intake duct beside the large molded chamber. The abbreviation means intake air temperature.

The useful detail is in the close-up. This little sensor has a twist-release mounting, so the drawing provides the choreography: release the tab, turn through the illustrated angle, then withdraw it. The instructions cover removal and reverse installation; they contain no sensor test or post-installation verification procedure.

items.name: Review before beginning the repair
items.detail: Carefully review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before beginning this repair, including its general service warnings. Before working on any listed system, also review that system’s safety reference linked there. These applicable linked references remain required reading; the selected precautions below do not replace that review. For work involving cooling fans, retain the referral to Engine Cooling System Health and Safety Precautions through that reference.

items.name: Disable remote start
items.detail: Before beginning this work around the vehicle, disable the remote start feature, if equipped, through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, potentially causing personal injury or death.

items.name: Remove the key
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service. An accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Account for auto start-stop equipment
items.detail: On vehicles with engine auto start-stop technology, the engine may start automatically with the ignition on. Make sure the ignition is off when servicing or working near rotating engine parts. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Check cooling fans before underhood work
items.detail: With the ignition OFF, inspect all cooling fans for damage, cracks or separation. Do not work under the hood with a damaged cooling fan; it can separate during operation. Replace a damaged fan with a new fan before proceeding. Failure to follow this instruction may result in serious personal injury. Fan replacement requires its own service instructions.

items.name: Disable fans before working nearby
items.detail: Cooling fans may run with the ignition off. Disable them before working nearby; ignition off alone is not protection against fan operation. Failure to disable them may result in personal injury. If this access requires nearby fan work, obtain the applicable fan-disabling instructions before proceeding.

items.name: Wear protective equipment
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to follow either precaution may result in serious personal injury.

edits.text: NOTE: The removal steps may also contain details needed during installation.
edits.why: Keep the illustrated release and rotation details in view during reassembly; installation reverses that movement.

edits.text: Locate the IAT sensor connector indicated in the first illustration and disconnect it from the sensor.
edits.why: Separating the plug leaves the sensor free to turn without carrying the attached wiring around with it.

edits.text: Press the retaining tab indicated in the close-up, turn the IAT sensor counterclockwise as viewed in that illustration through the angle shown in the inset, then withdraw the sensor from the intake duct.
edits.why: The tab and rotary movement release the sensor’s mounting. The inset supplies the required turn, making the removal more precise than simply pulling on the sensor.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: insert the IAT sensor into the intake duct, turn it back into its retained position, then reconnect the IAT sensor electrical connector.
edits.why: The mounting is restored before the electrical connection. Reversing the illustrated release movement returns the sensor to its secured position.
